Asian Games 2026: India Thrash Japan 49-24 In Men's Kabaddi Opener

India commenced their men's kabaddi campaign at the Asian Games 2026 with a resounding victory, overpowering Japan 49-24 in their opening fixture on Monday. The dominant performance sets a strong tone for the defending champions as they eye another gold medal in the prestigious continental event. This emphatic win reflects India's traditional prowess in the sport, where they have historically been a powerhouse.

From the outset, the Indian squad showcased superior raiding and defensive skills, quickly establishing a comfortable lead. Their cohesive teamwork and strategic plays proved too formidable for the Japanese side, who struggled to bridge the scoring gap throughout the match. The Indian raiders consistently secured points, while their defenders executed precise tackles, limiting Japan's offensive opportunities and ensuring a steady accumulation of points.

The significant margin of victory underscores India's preparedness and ambition for the tournament. This early triumph is crucial for building momentum and confidence within the team as they navigate the group stages against other competitive nations. The squad's depth and experience were evident, with multiple players contributing significantly to the scoreline, demonstrating a well-rounded performance.

This comprehensive win positions India favorably in their pool, demonstrating their intent to reclaim the top spot on the podium after a strong start. The team will now look to maintain this high level of performance and strategic execution in their subsequent matches as they progress deeper into the competition.

Vedaant, Actor R Madhavan's Son, Compares In His First Asian Games. Here's The Result

Indian swimmers Sajan Prakash, Dhakshan Shashikumar, Vedaant Madhavan, and Aneesh Sunil failed to qualify for the men's 4x200m freestyle relay final at the Asian Games. The quartet finished ninth among 13 competing teams in their heats, clocking a time of 7:24.32. This result means they will not advance to the medal round of the prestigious continental event.

The Indian relay team delivered a competitive performance but ultimately fell short of the top eight spots required to secure a place in the final. Despite their efforts, the time recorded was insufficient to challenge the leading nations in a highly competitive field. The race saw strong performances from teams across Asia, highlighting the high standard of swimming at the Games.

For Vedaant Madhavan, son of actor R Madhavan, this marks his debut appearance at the Asian Games. While the team did not progress, participating in such a major international multi-sport event provides invaluable experience for the young swimmer and his teammates. Competing at this level exposes athletes to intense competition and helps them gauge their performance against the continent's best.

The Indian contingent will now regroup and focus on other events at the Asian Games. Swimmers will aim to apply the lessons learned from this relay race to their individual events or future team competitions. The experience gained from this outing will be crucial for their continued development in the sport.

What to watch: Indian swimmers in their upcoming individual events at the Asian Games.
